The Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr alloy was prepared by vacuum/argon arc melting using high purity (99.9% or higher) elements.
After solidification on a water-cooled copper hearth, the alloy was hot iso-statically pressed (HIP’ d) at 1200 °C for 2 hours under a super-high purity argon pressure of 210 MPa.
After that it was homogenized by holding at 1200 °C for 24 h in a tube furnace with a continuous flow of high purity argon and then slow cooled at 10 °C/min. This condition is called Condition (1).

A piece of the sample in Condition (1) was sealed in a quartz tube filled with high purity argon and additionally annealed at 1400 °C for 20 min and water quenched. This condition is called Condition (2).

Another piece of the sample in Condition (2) was also sealed in a quartz tube filled with high purity argon and additionally annealed at 600 °C for 120 hrs and water quenched. This condition is called Condition (3).

The highlighted brighter regions, forming the continuous matrix, correspond to the ordered B2 phase while the darker discrete pockets correspond to the disordered BCC phase.
